profile.reading:
This building sits in the Krambeck Industrial Park in Sarpy County, part of the broader area around Google's original Nebraska data center campus in Papillion, which broke ground on 275 acres in late 2019 at a reported cost of roughly $600 million, Google's first Nebraska facility. Google has continued to expand the Papillion site and surrounding Sarpy County parcels in the years since, and a company spokesperson has described staff progression from Papillion into leadership roles at Google's newer Lincoln, Nebraska campus, illustrating how the original site anchored Google's broader Nebraska workforce. Since 2019, Google has created more than 120 jobs across computer technician, engineer, maintenance, and food service roles at its Nebraska sites, which the company has said it declines to break out by individual location. Google reports investing about $4.4 billion in Nebraska cumulatively over the five years through 2024, including $930 million in 2024 alone, spread across the Papillion, northwest Omaha, and Lincoln campuses. Google's own Nebraska data center location page does not identify which specific building in the Krambeck Industrial Park this OSM-mapped structure corresponds to, nor its individual square footage or MW capacity, so this registry records the $4.4 billion statewide figure as regional context rather than a fact specific to this building, and flags a Sarpy County Assessor parcel lookup as the next real research step.

Omaha Public Power District, which serves the Douglas and Sarpy county campuses, has cited large-load data center demand from Google and other operators as a leading factor in its own long-range generation and transmission planning, and Nebraska's status as one of the few states where electricity is delivered entirely by public power districts rather than investor-owned utilities has repeatedly come up in coverage of why Google, Facebook, and other hyperscalers chose the Omaha-Lincoln corridor for a dense cluster of campuses.

reading.body:
Google has invested $4.4 billion in Nebraska infrastructure over five years through 2024, with $930 million deployed in 2024 alone across the Papillion, northwest Omaha, and Lincoln campuses. This facility sits in the Krambeck Industrial Park near the original Papillion campus, which broke ground on 275 acres in late 2019 as Google's first Nebraska data center. The company does not publish individual building capacity or square footage for either campus, so the power consumption and rack density of this specific structure are not disclosed.

Google's Nebraska sites have created over 120 jobs in technical and support roles since 2019, and the company has described the Papillion location as a recruitment anchor that seeded leadership pipelines into its newer Lincoln campus. Omaha Public Power District, which serves both the Sarpy County and Douglas County Google facilities, identified large-load data center demand as a primary driver of its long-range generation and transmission planning. Nebraska's structure as a state served entirely by public power districts rather than investor-owned utilities has been cited repeatedly as a factor in Google's decision to concentrate multiple campuses in the Omaha-Lincoln corridor.

No published megawatt figure exists for this building, this campus, or any mapped facility in Nebraska. Among the 21 facilities mapped in Nebraska on this site, zero publish capacity specifications. The individual building-level power draw, square footage, and operational status of this structure remain unknown pending a Sarpy County Assessor parcel records lookup.
